sentences.text: Mr. Mukesh Shukla - Public Prosecutor for State.
Heard on admission.
Trial Court record perused.
Prima facie, this appeal seems to be arguable.
Hence, admitted for final hearing.

Further heard on I.A. No.495 of 2025 which is a first application under Section 430(1) of BNSS,
2023/389 of the CrPC, 1973 for suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

This Criminal Appeal assails the judgment dated 14.02.2023 passed by the learned Eighth Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District-Jabalpur (M.P.) in Sessions Trial No.323 of 2020,
whereby the appellant has been convicted under Sections 376 and 323 of the IPC and sentenced to undergo R.I. for 10 years and fine of Rs.500/- and R.I. for 03 months respectively, with default stipulation.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the the present appellant has pointed out that the trial Court has wrongly convicted the present appellant without proper appreciation of facts of the case.

entities.text: Eighth Additional Sessions Judge, Jabalpur, District-Jabalpur (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: It is contended that the present appellant has been in custody for more than five years as of today.
The FSL report is negative.
No external injuries were found on the person of 2 CRA-5322-2023 the prosecutrix.
Moreover, the prosecutrix was not previously acquainted with the accused and has categorically stated that she did not know the accused or even his name.
She has also admitted that the alleged incident occurred in the evening hours and that she has difficulty in seeing at night.
It is further submitted that the sister of the prosecutrix has not been examined by the prosecution nor have the seizure witnesses been examined.
Moreover, no Test Identification Parade of the present appellant was conducted by the prosecution, for reasons best known to it.
Keeping in view the contradictions/variations in the statements of witnesses as well as inherent infirmities in the prosecution case, he has a good case on merits.
It is further submitted that the present appeal will take considerable time for its disposal.
He is ready to comply with the conditions as may be imposed by this Court.
Looking to the period of custody, benefit of suspension of sentence may be granted and the appellant may be released on bail during pendency of this appeal.

sentences.text: On the other hand, learned counsel for the State has opposed the prayer made by the appellant.
Heard learned counsel for the rival parties and perused the record.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, but without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, I.A. No.495 of 2025 is allowed.

It is directed that subject to depositing the fine amount, if not already deposited, and on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand only) with a solvent surety of the like amount to the satisfaction of the concerned trial Court, the remaining jail sentence of the present appellant 3 CRA-5322-2023 shall remain suspended and he shall be released on bail.
The present appellant is further directed to mark his appearance before the concerned trial Court on 06.07.2026 and on subsequent dates as may be fixed by the trial Court in this regard.
List the case for final hearing in due course.
Certified copy as per rules.
